key_insight: RL2ML shows that finite-rollout training can be reframed as a family of surrogate objectives that exactly match the gradient of the sampled update, bridging reinforcement learning and maximum-likelihood-style training without objective-gradient mismatch.
engineering_relevance: For practical LLM training with limited rollout budgets, the framework helps choose update rules based on metric sensitivity and variance, not just on whether the objective looks more like RL or MLE.
method: Defines a continuum of finite-rollout surrogate objectives spanning RL, MLE-like, and beyond-MLE behavior.
Derives a closed-form, exactly unbiased gradient estimator aligned with the sampled rollout update.
Introduces group-level update scale and uses metric-gain plus variance analysis to reduce objective choice to a 1D optimization problem.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports calibrated metric-gain analysis and exact variance decomposition, showing the best surrogate depends jointly on evaluation metric, local sensitivity, and estimator variance.
watch_item: The framework is theoretically elegant, but selecting the optimal surrogate still requires reliable estimates of local metric sensitivity and variance, which may be noisy or task-dependent in practice.
paper_title: RL2ML: Finite-Rollout Surrogate Objectives from Reinforcement Learning to Maximum Likelihood
